classification.difficultyReason: Link equal tangents with segment addition/subtraction, and in part f identify the reflex central angle subtended by an obtuse circumference angle before applying quadrilateral and right-angle sums. The labelled construction supplies the representations for these familiar linked procedures.

content.prompt: Find the values of α, β, γ and θ, and the values of x, y and z. In the diagrams, tangents are drawn to the circle at S, T and U.

spec.description: Circle with centre O below exterior point P. Tangents PS and PT meet the circle at S on the upper left and T on the upper right. PS is labelled x; PT is labelled 5. Chord ST and radii OS and OT are drawn. Angle PST is 70°. α is angle STP; β is angle SPT; γ is angle TSO.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, construction lines and requested unknowns; no calculated values or proof conclusions added.

sizing.exceptionReason: The source tangent triangle has an essential40degree apex and separate20degree radius/chord sector. Preserve this proportion and readable10pt angle labels; a taller supplied figure is reviewed rather than compressed.

answer.worked: Tangents from P are equal, so $x=PS=PT=5$. Triangle PST is isosceles, hence $\alpha=70^\circ$ and $\beta=180^\circ-70^\circ-70^\circ=40^\circ$. Since OS is perpendicular to tangent PS, $\gamma=90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O to the left of exterior point A. Tangents AS and AT meet the circle at upper point S and lower point T. AS is labelled 8; AT is labelled x. Chord ST and radii OS and OT are drawn. Angle SAT is 40°. θ is angle SOT on the right of O; α is angle STA.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, construction lines and requested unknowns; no calculated values or proof conclusions added.

answer.worked: Tangents from A are equal, so $x=AT=AS=8$. Triangle AST is isosceles, giving $\alpha=\frac{(180^\circ-40^\circ)}{2}=70^\circ$. Both radius–tangent angles are $90^\circ$, so quadrilateral OSAT gives $\theta=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-40^\circ=140^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle BCA with an inscribed circle touching BC at S, CA at T and BA at U. B is at left, C at top and A at lower right. BS = 2, SC = 1, BU = x, UA = y and TA = z. An external double-ended dimension arrow labels the full length BA as 5.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, construction lines and requested unknowns; no calculated values or proof conclusions added.

answer.worked: Tangents from B are equal, so $x=BU=BS=2$. Then $y=UA=BA-BU=5-2=3$. Tangents from A are equal, so $z=AT=AU=3$.

spec.description: Triangle QRP with an inscribed circle touching QR at S, RP at T and QP at U. R is at top, Q at lower left and P at lower right. An external dimension arrow labels the full side QR as 11. Base portions QU and UP are labelled 4 and 6. The upper right-side portion RT is labelled x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, construction lines and requested unknowns; no calculated values or proof conclusions added.

sizing.exceptionReason: The full11 side dimension, two separate4/6 base portions and x on RT need distinct native10pt labels; preserve the source long-triangle proportions and required writing allowance if actual height exceeds40mm.

answer.worked: Tangents from Q are equal, so $QS=QU=4$. Hence $RS=QR-QS=11-4=7$. Tangents from R are equal, so $x=RT=RS=7$.

spec.description: Circle to the left of exterior point P. Upper tangent PS and lower tangent PT touch the circle at S and T. A vertical tangent touches the circle at U and intersects PS at B and PT at A. B, U and A are collinear in that order. BU = 4, UA = 5, BP = 10 and AP = x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, construction lines and requested unknowns; no calculated values or proof conclusions added.

answer.worked: Tangents from B are equal, so $BS=BU=4$. Thus $PS=PB+BS=10+4=14$. Tangents from P give $PT=PS=14$. Tangents from A give $AT=AU=5$, so $x=PA=PT-AT=14-5=9$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O. S lies on the left circumference, A on the upper-left circumference and T on the upper-right circumference. Exterior point P is above S. PS touches the circle at S; PT is drawn to T. Chords SA and AT and radii OS and OT are drawn. Angle SAT is 130° and angle ATO is 60°. α is the upper interior angle SOT; β is angle ASO; θ is angle PSA.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, construction lines and requested unknowns; no calculated values or proof conclusions added.

sizing.exceptionReason: Three close source angle sectors, supplied130/60 and separate tangent/chord/radius lines require readable native10pt text. Keep55mm width and inspect label-to-edge clearance without shrinking fonts.

answer.worked: The reflex central angle SOT on the same arc as $\angle SAT=130^\circ$ is $260^\circ$, so $\alpha=360^\circ-260^\circ=100^\circ$. In quadrilateral SATO, $\beta=360^\circ-130^\circ-60^\circ-100^\circ=70^\circ$. Since PS is perpendicular to OS, $\theta=90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ$.
